articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 11 2026 NFL Picks
articles.summary: NFL favorites are on a strong two-week run against the spread, but the tide could turn with five road underdogs getting at least 9.5 points on the Week 11 slate. Beware of backdoor covers in garbage time.
articles.body:
NFL favorites are on a strong two-week run against the spread, but the tide could turn with five road underdogs getting at least 9.5 points on the Week 11 slate. Beware of backdoor covers in garbage time.

Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , are always mindful of late covers for two-score lines, but they weren't afraid to lay a lot of points with home teams going against clubs with rookie or inexperienced starting quarterbacks.

The Houston Texans, Chicago Bears, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos are all favored by 9.5 or more points. How many of them cover a massive spread?

Before we dive into the matchups, check out our standings below. Knox has reached the .500 mark after back-to-back 10-win weeks. Hanford is right behind him with consecutive nine-win weeks. Moton is starting to look over his shoulder with a smaller lead.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Nov. 18, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Indianapolis Colts (3-7) at Houston Texans (3-6)

The Colts are struggling, but there's still a case for taking the underdog here.

Indianapolis has as many wins as the Texans, who just blew a 17-point lead in Cleveland. One of those wins by the Colts? Over Houston in Week 3. Laying double digits with the Texans is a bad idea.

The Texans understand they no longer have any margin for error after a 3-6 start, particularly after establishing a 17-0 halftime lead against the Cleveland Browns, only to lose. Fortunately, Houston gets to face the rudderless Colts.

The Texans have more than enough talent, particularly on offense this year, to easily overcome a double-digit spread considering the state of Indianapolis' defense.

Both of the Colts' top corners are injured, with Charvarius Ward already ruled out for Thursday's contest. Both of Indianapolis' starting tackles will also miss the game. Will Anderson Jr. should be licking his chops.

Texans: Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

New Orleans Saints (3-6) at Chicago Bears (7-2)

The Bears are coming off a bye here and at home in a matchup they should be able to handle fairly easily. I always pause at these double-digit spreads, but Jeffery Simmons has made a huge impact on the Bears defense.

The Saints will have a difficult time running the ball, and I don't trust Tyler Shough to keep pace with Caleb Williams, even with Jordyn Tyson in the fold.

Look for Williams to have a big game after a rough outing against Tampa Bay as the Bears win going away.

Well, 11.5 is a lot of points in an NFL game. The last time the Bears won at home by more than 11 points was back in Week 3 on Monday Night Football . The Bears are better than the Saints. The Bears will win this game. They're coming off a bye week, should be healthier, and have an offensive-minded coach who will certainly be looking to exploit the Saints' run defense.

The Saints have been better in that department lately, surrendering over 100 yards on the ground only once in their last four games. They're also 2-2 in that same stretch and have lost only one game by more than 11 points all season.

Oh, and New Orleans is also a league-best 3-0 ATS on the road this year. So, yeah, I'm taking the points.

Saints: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell

Baltimore Ravens (4-6) at Carolina Panthers (4-5)

Carolina is notorious for struggling to string together multiple wins during the Bryce Young era. In fact, going back to Young's rookie year of 2023, the Panthers are the league's second-worst team ATS after a win (6-11) and second-worst straight up (4-13) . Technically, given the 1.5-point spread, neither mark gives any confidence in the Panthers winning, let alone covering.

But the Ravens, losers of five straight and in complete freefall from their perennial playoff contender status, inspire even less confidence with Jacoby Brissett under center.

Brissett has a reputation for helping fantasy managers by feeding his receivers in garbage time, but this isn't fantasy football, and a 1.5-point spread doesn't leave much room for a backdoor cover.

This feels like an ugly one-point win for one of these teams, desperate for any sort of momentum at this point in the season.

The Ravens' offense looked listless even with new QB Jacoby Brissett at the helm on Monday night. The Panthers struggled to throw the ball in their win over the Saints, but Chuba Hubbard's tough running lets this team grind when it needs to.

I'm expecting both defenses to play fairly well here, and both QBs to struggle through the air. Carolina will move the ball well enough on the ground to earn a one-point win.

Ravens: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Miami Dolphins (1-8) at Buffalo Bills (8-1)

Miami Dolphins' second-year quarterback Kyle McCord is set to make his second career start on the road against the Buffalo Bills, who have covered this spread in three consecutive games. Understandably, 70 percent of bets via Action Network are on Buffalo.

However, it's important to factor in Buffalo's upcoming Thanksgiving matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Bills may take their foot off the gas pedal, allowing the feisty young Dolphins to score late for a backdoor cover on a massive spread. Miami has covered in five of its last six games.

A three-score spread is the only reason to even consider the Dolphins in this particular matchup. Even then, it's not enough.

Kyle McCord won't be able to keep pace with Josh Allen. Plus, Buffalo features a different caliber of defense compared to Miami's previous opponent, the Indianapolis Colts.

Since the Bills' bye in Week 7, Jim Leonhard's unit has allowed only 28 points during the subsequent three contests.

Bills: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski

Tennessee Titans (1-8) at Dallas Cowboys (4-6)

Earlier in the season, I probably would have backed the Cowboys laying 7.5 points in this matchup without hesitation. However, two factors are pushing me in the opposite direction in Week 11.

For one, Dallas' defense is just as bad as it was a year ago, if not worse. At this point, it's hard to envision the Cowboys blowing out any opponent that doesn't also reside in the mediocre NFC East because of that defense. Dallas has been especially vulnerable against the run, which is a particular problem against a Titans team ranked 10th in yards per carry.

Secondly, Tennessee has finally started to complement its ground game with a functional passing attack. Cam Ward still isn't playing up to his draft status, but he's helped the Titans top 300 total yards in three straight games.

I do think the Cowboys win this one, but it'll be close.

The Cowboys' two blowout wins this year came against division opponents starting backup quarterbacks. Tennessee isn't a division rival, but Dallas will look to exploit another favorable quarterback matchup against Cam Ward.

Tennessee should be able to run the ball against the Cowboys' league-worst rush defense; however, the Titans have the league's worst pass defense and face Dallas' third-ranked passing offense. I don't see Tennessee hanging around in a shootout on the road.

Cowboys: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Arizona Cardinals (3-7) at Kansas City Chiefs (7-2)

With four of this week's 13 games featuring spreads above 11 points, at least one of those picks seems bound to come back to bite us—and I'm taking the underdogs in three of them.

To be clear, the Chiefs are going to cruise at Arrowhead against a bad Arizona team with a rookie quarterback. But teams that are cruising take their foot off the gas, and the Cardinals are 4-2 ATS on the road this season.

As in the Bills–Dolphins matchup, the massive spread makes taking the points tempting.

But the difference is, the Dolphins have been competitive regardless of opponent over the past month, and the Cardinals have scored nine points over the last two weeks, six with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center in the previous outing.

Furthermore, due to the Cardinals' injuries and the departure of Marvin Harrison Jr. via trade, Beck's top wide receiver in catches and receiving yards is Devin Duvernay, who's also the team's top kick and punt returner.

Even if Kenneth Walker III sits out consecutive games, the Chiefs rout the Cardinals at home by 16 or more points.

Chiefs: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) at Detroit Lions (7-2)

In a week littered with massive spreads, the Lions giving less than a touchdown at home against Tampa is puzzling. Perhaps Vegas has set a trap. But the Buccaneers may struggle to exploit Detroit's vulnerable pass defense, especially with Baker Mayfield's availability uncertain.

The Bucs won't be able to lean on the ground game against Detroit's fifth-ranked run defense, and the Lions can't afford a post-Germany letdown in the fiercely competitive NFC North. Detroit wins this one by two touchdowns—at least.

With Baker Mayfield (foot/ankle) ailing, this is a problematic matchup for the Buccaneers. Tampa's offense is built to lead with the run, and the Lions happen to be quite effective at stopping opposing ball-carriers.

However, defense travels, and Tampa's has been terrific this season. We saw that a couple of weeks ago when the Buccaneers stymied the Chicago Bears and nearly pulled off the road upset. The Bucs are also coming off of their bye and have had extra time to game plan for the Lions.

Detroit's defense, meanwhile, just lost its best player when Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in Germany. His absence will be felt both on the field and in the locker room.

Tampa might not be a great team, but it's been a tough out all season. The Bucs have only lost one game by more than six points this season, and that was a seven-point loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3.

Buccaneers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-7)

The Steelers defense did not play well against Joe Burrow and the Bengals last week, but this is a spot where the unit should bounce back.

The Eagles have been decimated by injuries on both sides of the ball, but the offense, especially, is a shell of itself. Jaylen Warren and the Steelers' run game should have an easier time getting going against a run defense that's struggled all season, giving Aaron Rodgers more room to work.

The Steelers need a bounce-back win here, and they get it by a touchdown.

The Eagles have the luxury of playing at home while coming off their bye week. Plus, the roster is getting healthier. Wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, as well as linebacker Jihaad Campbell, were all on the practice field this week.

Those potential lineup additions—especially the wide receivers—make this matchup far more intriguing, particularly if Saquon Barkley can get going and draw Pittsburgh's safeties into the box. Pittsburgh isn't an explosive team, particularly on offense. The Eagles will have every opportunity to keep this game close.

Steelers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

New York Jets (2-8) at Los Angeles Chargers (1-8)

If Geno Smith's ankle injury sidelines him in Week 11, this pick isn't going to age well. But the Jets quarterback is expected to be OK, and if that's the case, take the points.

That we're living in a world where Smith is more reliable under center than Justin Herbert is unsettling. But that's where we are—even in last week's win, Herbert threw for all of 129 yards. The Jets are bad, but the Chargers are worse. So again, take the points.

The Chargers won a game this week. If they win one this coming weekend, that's two in a row. If they can then beat the New England Patriots, that's called a winning streak. It has happened before. The possibility would prove to be a nice reversal after an 0-8 start to the season. It's possible, too.

The Chargers have to take care of business at home against the Jets, though. They'll either get to face a banged-up Geno Smith or fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik. Either way, Los Angeles has a legitimate opportunity to win back-to-back games for the first time since the middle of last December.

Chargers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) at Denver Broncos (7-2)

The scoring margin gap between these two teams is only 5.1 points per game, as the Broncos have won by double digits just once this season. This Raiders team is also much more competitive than the one that was only outscored by 10 total points in two matchups with Denver in 2025. I expect the Broncos to win, but by a single score.

In Week 10, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza looked sharp for a little more than a quarter with Brock Bowers on the field, but that changed in the second half without the All-Pro tight end.

Bowers suffered an ankle injury and exited the game after trying to play through it early in the second quarter.

On Monday, head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters that the tight end avoided a major injury, but it's still "significant," and the team will monitor him throughout the week.

The Raiders run their one-dimensional offense through Bowers. He's Mendoza's best pass-catcher and safety blanket. Without him or a reliable rushing attack, the rookie could have a tough outing against the Broncos, who are coming off a bye week.

Of course, if Bowers plays, the Raiders can keep the score within 10 points in a matchup with a familiar opponent. So, his availability is key to the side on this spread.

Broncos: Davenport, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) at New York Giants (5-3-1)

The Jaguars have been feasting on competition that has barely put up a fight. The Ravens are in a free fall, while the Colts and Titans were already selling off parts when Jacksonville blew both out.

The challenge should be much different against a spunky Giants squad that is unlikely to go down easily while trying to avoid a third consecutive home loss. New York is coming off a mini-bye here, and the weather at MetLife could also be an equalizing factor.

The Giants lose games they should win and then show up in games they're supposed to lose. In fact, there's probably no more startling statistic, even with the league's second-weakest schedule to date, than the Giants' 6-3 ATS mark this year. No matter what I pick here, the Giants will somehow break my heart.

The Jaguars are looking to stake a claim as a legitimate Super Bowl favorite, and at less than a touchdown, I'll buy that here. Two of the Giants' three ATS losses have been at home; MetLife Stadium has never been a genuine home-field advantage for this organization, and it's time to stop forgetting that J.J. McCarthy is playing QB for the overachieving G-Men, not Jaxson Dart. Jacksonville with a statement win on the road.

Jaguars: Davenport, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Minnesota Vikings (7-2) vs. San Francisco 49ers (8-1)

Back in Week 1, the 49ers took an early trip to Australia to acclimate, while the Rams decided on a condensed last-minute journey. The Niners won that game handily and have largely looked like the top team in the NFL since.

This past Sunday, the 49ers flew to Denver for high-altitude preparation for Sunday's showdown in Mexico City. The Vikings have decided to stay in Minnesota before flying into Mexico this weekend.

Could well-planned preparation give San Francisco the edge once again? Perhaps, but I still like the Vikings here. Minnesota's defense has been the best in the NFL, and the addition of Kirk Cousins has created a balanced Super Bowl contender.

I'm aware that Cousins just threw three interceptions against San Francisco as the Raiders' starter in Week 9. However, he also came in on short notice and helped the Vikings blow out a very good Packers team in Week 10. I'll trust him to be better in this oddity of a rematch.

The Vikings and 49ers will travel to Mexico City for this game. On a neutral field, it should be an even matchup.

In his first outing back with the Vikings, Cousins elevated the team's passing attack, and Minnesota scored 30, the most since its 39-22 Week 1 win over the Packers.

That said, the Vikings have been susceptible to ground attacks lately, allowing 134 or more rushing yards in three of their last four contests. Under head coach Kyle Shanahan, the 49ers have been one of the best at running the ball, and they can do it with Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black, both averaging 4.5 yards per carry.

With the spread this tight, I'll take the team with the clear advantage.

49ers: Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) at Washington Commanders (3-5-1)

Washington has had extra time to prepare for a Cincinnati team that could be walking into a bit of a trap on the road. With a healthy Jayden Daniels this season, the Commanders haven't lost a game by more than a single score. Washington is in a desperate spot at home, and this team doesn't look as though it is ready to give up on 2026 just yet.

This one is pretty simple for me. The Commanders rank 31st in the league in passing yards allowed and have allowed opposing QBs to complete over 65 percent of their passes. That doesn't bode well against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, who just demolished a Steelers defense that came in red-hot.

Beating the Bengals right now is likely going to require a team that can go score-for-score with them as Burrow picks apart your secondary, at least to a degree, and Washington doesn't have the firepower to do that. Bengals win this one by double digits.

Bengals: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for USC OT Elijah Paige
articles.summary: Elijah Paige is a broadly built, smooth-moving left tackle with an NFL frame, efficient pass-set mechanics, and enough functional athleticism to cover significant space without wasted movement. He combines patient hands and length with encouraging anchor strength, while his initial force and movement ability also translate in the run game. His biggest issue is sustaining control after first contact, where overextension and lagging feet can leave him vulnerable to counters and late sheds.
articles.body:
Elijah Paige is a broadly built, smooth-moving left tackle with an NFL frame, efficient pass-set mechanics, and enough functional athleticism to cover significant space without wasted movement. He combines patient hands and length with encouraging anchor strength, while his initial force and movement ability also translate in the run game. His biggest issue is sustaining control after first contact, where overextension and lagging feet can leave him vulnerable to counters and late sheds.

Paige is a 6'7", 315-pound offensive line prospect who arrived at USC as a 4-star recruit in the 2023 class. He made one start at left tackle as a true freshman in 2023 before starting all 13 games there in 2024. He started seven games at left tackle in 2025 while dealing with injuries throughout the season and returned as USC's starting left tackle in 2026.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Smooth lateral-to-vertical pass sets with very little wasted motion, allowing him to efficiently reach his set points while maintaining balance and inside-out leverage.

Patient hand usage with the length and grip strength to engulf rushers, refit and widen the high-side path once attached.

Encouraging anchor against direct power, showing the ability to absorb momentum, throw his hips back, and abruptly halt bull rushes without consistently conceding the integrity of the pocket.

Functional athlete in the run game with good short-area range, combo timing and second-level anticipation. Generates meaningful initial force on doubles and can execute backside cutoffs and overtakes.

Drive-phase sustain is inconsistent. His initial surge can be impressive, but his feet occasionally stop or lag behind his upper body, creating overextension and allowing defenders to redirect or shed him late.

Can lose balance or require late recovery against inside counters when his weight gets too far forward, particularly after initially committing to the outside threat.

Anchor is functional but not completely dominant, as stronger power rushes can compress him before he settles. Exchange recognition against movement also needs further evaluation.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Athletic LT prospect with the frame, body control, and pass protection tools to start as a rookie and develop into an above-average, high-quality starter on the blindside .

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Alabama Edge Yhonzae Pierre
articles.summary: Yhonzae Pierre has the size, strength, and athleticism NFL teams want in a premier edge rusher. His ability to turn speed-to-power is unmatched in the 2026 NFL draft class, and his traits give him a high ceiling at the next level. However, the Alabama product does need to refine his technique to reach his potential.
articles.body:
Yhonzae Pierre has the size, strength, and athleticism NFL teams want in a premier edge rusher. His ability to turn speed-to-power is unmatched in the 2026 NFL draft class, and his traits give him a high ceiling at the next level. However, the Alabama product does need to refine his technique to reach his potential.

Despite being a 5-star recruit and the 31st-ranked player overall in the 2023 high school class, Pierre didn't see the field much until his redshirt sophomore season. He had a strong performance during that campaign, collecting 52 tackles, 14.5 for loss and eight sacks in 15 games to become the Crimson Tide's top pass-rusher.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Pierre has good size and a good frame for a line of scrimmage linebacker, and appears to have long arms.

Quick to react to the snap and accelerates off the line to put pressure on offensive tackles as a pass-rusher.

Combination of acceleration and change-of-direction skills makes him very good at turning speed-to-power off the edge.

Impressive upper body strength to push the pocket with a long-arm move or push an offensive tackle's inside shoulder.

Quick and agile to be an effective looper on line games.

Comfortable dropping into coverage; had an impressive pick-six in the 2026 season opener against East Carolina.

Has the strength to beat and shed blocks against tight ends in the running game.

Will be able to hold his own against offensive tackles if he gets his hands up faster and plays with better pad level/knee bend as a run defender.

Pierre isn't a refined pass-rusher yet, often relying on his natural gifts to win rather than setting up his moves or using his hands.

Subpar bend to turn tight corners at the top of the rush.

Struggles with his balance when rushing the passer, often getting knocked to the ground when linemen get their hands on him.

Against the run, he's late to get his hands up and plays with little knee bend, leading to issues holding ground against base blocks from bigger offensive tackles.

Also struggles to set the edge versus pullers.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Line of Scrimmage Linebacker (Khalil Mack to Boye Mafe)

Workout numbers and data will be added at a later date.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for South Carolina OT Jacarrius Peak
articles.summary: Jacarrius Peak is a strong-handed, physical blocker whose grip strength and ability to strain through contact give him a cleaner NFL projection inside than at tackle. He is at his best when he can reduce space, get square to his target, and use his heavy hands to control the point of attack, while his vertical-set approach has helped compensate for limited lateral quickness on the edge. Inconsistent balance, redirect ability and foot/hip synchronization restrict his range in space, making guard the better projection despite his extensive college tackle experience.
articles.body:
Jacarrius Peak is a strong-handed, physical blocker whose grip strength and ability to strain through contact give him a cleaner NFL projection inside than at tackle. He is at his best when he can reduce space, get square to his target, and use his heavy hands to control the point of attack, while his vertical-set approach has helped compensate for limited lateral quickness on the edge. Inconsistent balance, redirect ability and foot/hip synchronization restrict his range in space, making guard the better projection despite his extensive college tackle experience.

Peak is a 6'4", 305-pound offensive line prospect who arrived at NC State as a 4-star recruit in the 2022 class. He did not play as a true freshman before making six starts at right tackle in 2023 and starting all 13 games there in 2024. Peak moved to left tackle and started all 12 games in 2025 before transferring to South Carolina, where he has continued to play left tackle in 2026.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Heavy hands and legitimate grip strength allow him to clamp, stay attached, and strain through contact. Once he establishes a secure fit, he's hard to disengage from cleanly and can use that grip to steer or finish defenders.

Stout when he can square up and play through his frame. His better down blocks, post blocks, and direct-contact reps show enough functional strength to absorb force, reestablish leverage, and secure the point of attack.

Developed a useful pass-protection approach built around vertical sets and flash/bait techniques. Reducing space lets him force rushers into his frame, disrupt their timing, and maximize his hand strength instead of exposing him to extended lateral movement.

Competitive blocker who consistently strains to sustain and finish. His physicality and effort give him a chance to salvage imperfect positioning and should translate favorably to the tighter confines of guard.

Lateral quickness and redirect ability are limiting traits. His movements can become elongated and laborious when defenders change direction, with his feet frequently arriving late and leaving him vulnerable to inside counters or second-level movement.

Body control deteriorates when his lower half gets out of phase with his hands. He will lean, overextend, or allow his hips to swing behind the block, creating compromised positions and forcing him to rely too heavily on his grip to sustain.

Processing and control against movement need more consistency. He has shown late takeover footwork on combinations and can become tunnel-visioned against games, while defenders who establish first meaningful contact can pry him open or stack him before he recovers.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Strong-handed developmental guard with legitimate grip, strain and point-of-attack sturdiness whose limited lateral quickness and body control are better protected inside.

Workout numbers and data will be added at a later date.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Michigan CB Jyaire Hill
articles.summary: Jyaire Hill has the tools and movement skills to excel in any scheme he plays, thanks to his natural athletic ability, aggressiveness, and "next play" mentality that every corner needs to succeed. He blows up screens with quick trigger and play recognition, navigating under and around blocks with a finisher's aggression. His frame is exactly what NFL coaches want, with long arms to impact the catch point whenever he's close.
articles.body:
Jyaire Hill has the tools and movement skills to excel in any scheme he plays, thanks to his natural athletic ability, aggressiveness, and "next play" mentality that every corner needs to succeed. He blows up screens with quick trigger and play recognition, navigating under and around blocks with a finisher's aggression. His frame is exactly what NFL coaches want, with long arms to impact the catch point whenever he's close.

The former 4-star recruit looks more filled out than he did a season ago, adding to his desire to be a physical player in every phase. Hill brings a fire to the defense that is easy to see and appreciate, even if he needs to rein it in every now and then.

Dan has covered the Kansas City Chiefs and the NFL Draft since 2019 while contributing for RGR Football. Most recently, he spent the 2025 draft cycle at The Draft Network and is entering his first season in our scouting department.

Hill has experience in a multitude of techniques, but does his best work as a cover three corner with above-average zone eyes.

Play identification happens quickly, particularly in the run/screen game, and when he puts his foot in the ground, he flies downhill.

He's a unique athlete at his size and has the frame and length to compete down the field when the ball is in the air.

The 6'2", 190-pound corner reads the quarterback well and matches route combinations at a high level.

His use of physicality and the sideline as a boundary corner shows up on fade routes and go balls downfield.

Hill tends to focus on hitting the ball carrier and not tackling, especially when triggering downhill, which leads to missed tackles.

He struggles with down-to-down consistency and shows mental lapses too often.

His physicality will get the better of him at the top of routes, leading to penalties that extend drives.

Michigan's Defensive Skill Player of the Year in 2025 will get beat in soft-press by giving up too much ground inside. Needs to work on patience.

PLAYSTYLE FAMILY : Hill profiles best as a zone (cover three) corner with the capability to play many techniques. In the Tyson Campbell bucket of cornerbacks.

Workout numbers and data will be added at a later date .

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes reveals what Josh Downs did to win his trust, hinting at a promising Chiefs connection: "He’s a smart guy”
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes may have found another reliable target in Josh Downs.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes may have found another reliable target in Josh Downs. The Kansas City Chiefs receiver made an encouraging first impression against the Atlanta Falcons, catching five passes for 53 yards and a touchdown despite playing only 10 offensive snaps. Mahomes was impressed, but one particular play caught his attention more than the numbers. The quarterback also admitted that a lack of familiarity with Downs' understanding of the playbook initially held him back from throwing his way. That hesitation may not last long.Patrick Mahomes was impressed by Josh Downs' understanding of the playbookThe Chiefs needed a strong passing performance, and their 30-?? showing against Atlanta offered some encouragement. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns, spreading the ball among four different receivers. Downs gave the offense another option, even though he had spent limited time learning the system.His debut could have been even better. Mahomes revealed that he noticed Downs making the right reads during the game, including on a two-minute drill play that the pair had not practised together. The quarterback liked what he saw, but admitted he was not entirely sure whether the receiver knew his assignment.“I knew by talking to him that he was a smart guy and he was going to be able to pick up this stuff,” Mahomes said. “I thought the most impressive one (catch) was the two-minute play where he was able to go out there and run the route. That was stuff we hadn’t worked on. If I would have trusted that, I would have thrown him the ball, but in the back of my head I didn’t know for sure if he knew what route he has. But he did exactly what he was supposed to do. He’s a true pro. He’s spending the extra time in here, with coaches, and with me, and learning fast. He’s a smart guy.”That admission says quite a bit about how quickly Downs is adjusting. Mahomes did not simply praise the receiver's athletic ability. He pointed to his preparation and understanding of the offense, two things that can make a difference when a new player joins a team during the season.Josh Downs could see a bigger role as chemistry developsDowns' five receptions from just 10 offensive snaps offer another reason for the Chiefs to feel encouraged. His involvement was limited, but he made the most of those opportunities. More importantly, Mahomes believes the receiver was getting open on plays that never came his way.That could change as the two spend more time working together. Mahomes highlighted Downs' ability to adjust to the ball, recognise open spaces and create separation through his routes. Those qualities give the quarterback more options when a play breaks down or the defence takes away his first read.“He’s got a great feel,” Mahomes said. “He does a great job of adjusting to the football. Understanding where he’s open, setting himself up with routes. Looking at the tape, he got open even more than I gave him opportunities for. He knows how to get himself open and to run routes. As we build more trust and chemistry on the football field, he’ll get more opportunities.”For Kansas City, the bigger question is how quickly Downs can become a regular part of the passing attack. His debut suggests he has already earned Mahomes' attention. If that trust continues to grow, the receiver could have a much larger role in the Chiefs' plans over the coming weeks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Marlon Humphrey Sent Home by Ravens, Out vs. Panthers After Comments on City of Baltimore
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home, and he'll miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home, and he'll miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.

Coach Jesse Minter said he and the "leadership of the organization" made the collective decision to deactivate Humphrey for one game. He also described the player as "very remorseful."

Humphrey drew the quick condemnation of Ravens fans and residents of Baltimore when he suggested on his podcast the city is the "best at making criminals."

The four-time Pro Bowler quickly apologized:

Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott responded that the public statement was "not enough."

"Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper," he said.

Scott included a subtle shot at Humphrey's performance when he said Baltimore "recently lost our way" after having "once produced great defensive backs."

Sidelining Humphrey for this week is a bold call when the Ravens are 4-6 and riding a five-game losing streak. They can ill afford to cede any more ground in the AFC playoff race.

Humphrey is headed for free agency in the offseason. While he's bound to suit up again for Baltimore, presumably in Week 12 against the Houston Texans, his remarks may have all but assured he'll be playing elsewhere in 2027.

articles.title: John Harbaugh shuts down Jaguars’ NFL dominance talk with brutal ‘I could care less’ response before Giants clash
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh brushed aside talk about the Jacksonville Jaguars’ place among the NFL’s best teams, saying he cares more about
articles.body: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh brushed aside talk about the Jacksonville Jaguars’ place among the NFL’s best teams, saying he cares more about what they show on the field than outside opinions. Harbaugh made the comments on Wednesday, November 18, before the Giants host the 7-2 Jaguars in Week 11. New York enters the game at 5-3-1, with kickoff set for Sunday at MetLife Stadium.John Harbaugh gives blunt response to questions about Jacksonville Jaguars’ successAsked what has helped Jacksonville become one of the league’s top teams, Harbaugh did not spend time discussing rankings or outside analysis. Instead, he made clear that his focus was on the team New York will face this weekend.“I don’t care. I could care less. That sort of analysis about why they’re where, or one of our opponents. We don’t even look at that. All you do is you look at the team they are right now, the opponent that we’re facing,” Harbaugh said, according to the New York Giants’ official website.He then praised Jacksonville’s strength across the field, pointing to its defense, offense and special teams. He also spoke highly of quarterback Trevor Lawrence and the team’s offensive line, describing it as big and strong while recognising the talent around Lawrence.When asked about Jacksonville’s record, he brought up former coach Bill Parcells’ well-known line: “You are what your record says you are.” The Jaguars are 7-2.Jacksonville has won three games in a row, including a 40-23 road victory over the Tennessee Titans on November 15. The NFL’s Week 11 team capsules rank Jacksonville fourth in scoring and second in points allowed. The Jaguars are averaging 29.9 points per game while giving up just 16 points on average.Harbaugh also discussed changes to Jacksonville’s defense. The Jaguars recently added defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III in trades. Both players are expected to make their team debuts against the Giants. Harbaugh said New York would study the players who are now available, but he did not expect the changes to alter how Jacksonville runs its defense.John Harbaugh explains what the Jaguars game means for the New York GiantsThe Giants are 5-3-1 and lead the NFC East, but their latest outing ended in a 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders. A win over Jacksonville would help them protect their place in the division as the schedule gets tougher.Harbaugh made it clear that he does not see the Jaguars as unbeatable, even with their strong record. He said, “The so-called heavyweights, I’ve seen them play bad games too.” When asked if New York might take more risks to get the win, he replied, “We’re gonna do whatever’s necessary to win the football game. Sometimes it looks like it, sometimes it doesn’t.”The Giants now face a demanding stretch, with games against Jacksonville, Indianapolis, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland and Detroit ahead. Their offense will need to produce more consistently against teams that can challenge them on both sides of the ball.Sunday’s game is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium. articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Oregon DL A'Mauri Washington
articles.summary: A'Mauri Washington would have been a fringe first-round pick in last year's draft before he opted to return to school, but he still has the potential to be one of the top defensive tackles in the 2027 class.
articles.body:
A'Mauri Washington would have been a fringe first-round pick in last year's draft before he opted to return to school, but he still has the potential to be one of the top defensive tackles in the 2027 class.

Standing at 6'6" and 325 pounds with plenty of strength and impressive movement skills for his size, giving Washington the traits that NFL teams will be enamoured with. For context, he was listed as the third-best athlete on Bruce Feldman's list this summer, hitting 20.7 mph and recording a 35-inch vertical jump, along with impressive weight room numbers.

A 4-star recruit in the 2023 high school class, the Oregon product didn't see much field time behind Brandon Dorlus (2024 fourth-round pick), Derrick Harmon (2025 first-round pick), and Jamaree Caldwell (2025 third-round pick) during his first two years on campus.

Washington enjoyed a breakout campaign during his junior year, though, racking up 33 tackles, 4.5 for loss, a sack and eight passes defended to earn Third-Team All-Big Ten honors.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Washington has good size and appears to have decent arm length.

Impressive get-off and quick off the ball to get penetration, especially when slanting.

Very good strength at the point of attack to gain control of one-on-one blocks, stand up offensive linemen and hold his gap.

Has also shown the quickness and agility to beat linemen across their faces and make the tackle in the adjacent gap, effectively taking away two rushing lanes.

Little to no issues escaping blocks from offensive linemen to make tackles near the line of scrimmage. Also is good at catching offensive linemen leaning and shedding blocks with a hump move.

Solid power as a pass-rusher to occasionally collapse the pocket with a bull rush when he keeps his pads down.

Has the strength and violence to develop a push-pull move, had a win with it against Boise State using just one arm.

Athletic ability gives him the potential to grow as a pass-rusher if his use of hands improves.

Gets his hands up as a pass-rusher to bat passes at the line of scrimmage.

Alignment and scheme versatility, he can play anywhere from a 4i-technique to 1-technique/shade nose tackle.

Washington has a tendency to play with high pad level, causing him to get pushed out of his gap against combo blocks/double teams.

Also needs to add rotational strength to avoid getting his shoulders turned when taking on scoop blocks.

Block recognition against the run is lacking, leading to him getting reached, scooped or caught off guard by double teams.

Hand placement is a little wide when taking on blocks against the run, exposing his chest against offensive linemen who play with tight hands.

Use of hands as a pass-rusher is a work in progress; he's often late and inaccurate with his hands or chops when starting pass-rush moves, allowing offensive linemen to make the first significant contact frequently.

Also doesn't work the offensive lineman's hands after contact.

Hasn't shown a go-to pass-rush move that he can win consistently with right now, nor does he work counter moves if his initial move isn't effective. Needs to rush with more of a plan.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Versatile interior defensive lineman (Vita Vea to Eddie Goldman)

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Kentucky IOL Coleton Price
articles.summary: Coleton Price is a stout, strength-first center with a sturdy anchor, good hand usage and a natural feel for sorting interior movement. He can absorb power, provide force as a helper and generate torque once attached, but his feet and balance become less reliable when defenders force sudden redirection. Price projects as a developmental interior contributor with enough physicality and processing to compete for a starting role, though his movement limitations narrow the margin.
articles.body:
Coleton Price is a stout, strength-first center with a sturdy anchor, good hand usage and a natural feel for sorting interior movement. He can absorb power, provide force as a helper and generate torque once attached, but his feet and balance become less reliable when defenders force sudden redirection. Price projects as a developmental interior contributor with enough physicality and processing to compete for a starting role, though his movement limitations narrow the margin.

Price is a 6'3", 308-pound offensive line prospect who entered Baylor as a 3-star recruit in the 2022 class. He redshirted in 2022 before making the final six starts of the 2023 season at center, then started all 13 games there in 2024. Price made 11 starts at center in 2025 while dealing with injuries before transferring to Kentucky, where he became the starting center in 2026.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Brings good play strength and a stout lower half to absorb force, establish his anchor and remain firm when he gets square.

Shows good awareness and processing against pressure and defensive-line movement, with the eyes and timing to pass threats, collect loopers and sort mugged or overloaded fronts.

Uses tight, independent hands to establish leverage, disrupt rushers and provide force as an uncovered helper.

Generates torque and finishing power once attached, with the grip and core strength to turn or dump defenders when he establishes leverage.

Short-area redirection can be stressed by sudden interior movement, particularly when a defender gets him leaning before changing direction.

Balance deteriorates when his weight distribution gets too far outside his frame, leaving him vulnerable to stutters, clubs and quick moves across his face.

Range is functional rather than a defining strength, creating a smaller margin on difficult back blocks, extended reaches and recoveries against quick interior defenders.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Stout, strength-first center with good processing, anchor and torque whose movement and redirection limitations temper his starting ceiling.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Miami DL Justin Scott
articles.summary: Justin Scott has the size (6'4" and 303 pounds) and strength to be an effective run-defending defensive tackle in the NFL. However, his pass-rush skills leave something to be desired, and he's had an underwhelming 2026 season.
articles.body:
Justin Scott has the size (6'4" and 303 pounds) and strength to be an effective run-defending defensive tackle in the NFL. However, his pass-rush skills leave something to be desired, and he's had an underwhelming 2026 season.

A 5-star recruit and the No. 10 player overall in the 2024 high school class, Scott was a backup defensive lineman in his first year at Miami. He broke out during the Hurricanes' 2025 National Championship run the following year, playing in 15 games (nine starts) and collecting 26 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss and a sack .

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Scott has good size for an NFL defensive tackle and reportedly has long arms (33 inches, according to On3 Sports ).

Has violent hands and plenty of upper body strength to generate knockback power and stand-up offensive linemen when taking on blocks against the run.

Plays with a wide base and has the strength to anchor against base blocks from interior offensive linemen.

Gets a lot of extension on blocks with his strength and length combination, making it easier for him to shed or escape.

Enough quickness and agility to cross the offensive lineman's face and make tackles in the adjacent gap.

Has experience playing as either a shade nose tackle or 3-technique and has been a good run defender from both alignments.

Hustle player who can factor into gang tackles down the field.

Scott has minimal pass rush production with just two career sacks, as of Oct. 19, and doesn't show many pass-rush skills to build on.

Inconsistent get-off and pad level limit the effectiveness of his bull rush.

Often late with his hands when rushing the passer and doesn't work the offensive lineman's hands after contact.

Shows lower body stiffness, making it difficult to get clean wins with finesse moves as a pass-rusher.

Subpar pass-rush motor and doesn't work counter moves.

Has trouble sinking his hips to anchor against down blocks and double teams/combo blocks. Doesn't anticipate doubles well, either.

Lacks the lateral movement skills and block recognition to avoid getting reached consistently.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Run-Stuffing DT (Kawann Short to A'Shawn Robinson)

articles.title: Tyran Stokes injury update: Will Kansas star play in Players Era title game?
articles.summary: Tyran Stokes' status for Kansas vs. Houston in the Players Era 8 championship game remains up in the air.
articles.body:
Kansas' men's basketball has the chance to win one of the most prominent early season tournaments, but will it have its star for it?

Freshman guard Tyran Stokes is uncertain for the Players Era 8 championship game against Houston on Thursday, Nov. 19 as he deals with a bone bruise in his leg , which he suffered early in the tournament. It already resulted in him missing the semifinal games against West Virginia, which the Jayhawks narrowly held on to win.

Now facing another Big 12 contender in Houston for the tournament title, Kansas could use its star to make one of the biggest statements in the first month of the season.

See who dominates Nielsen's list of top college basketball fan bases

Stokes is day-to-day and will likely be a game-time decision, coach Bill Self said after the win over West Virginia.

It's the same designation Stokes had against the Mountaineers, as the team said he would take part in pre-game warm-ups before a decision was made. He warmed up, but sat on the bench for the entire game. Self explained the decision was not his.

"The whole deal was, he was going to warm up and if he felt like that he didn't have to favor his leg, he was going to play. Because he got the clearance to do that," Self said. "But, he didn't feel that way. He struggled with that. Maybe he'll feel better tomorrow, it's day-to-day, but still the reports we got were more favorable than maybe what we thought they would be yesterday."

Stokes suffered the injury during the opening-round game of the Players Era against UNLV on Tuesday, Nov. 17.

Early in the second half, he collided with a UNLV player for a loose ball after a missed free throw. While nothing looked out of the ordinary, when he passed the ball he started to hobble and then sat down on the court, pointing to his right knee.

A trainer came onto the court and helped him walk off the court and into the locker room, sitting out the remainder of the win.

Kansas could use Stokes considering the immediate impact he has made for the Jayhawks.

The top recruit in the 2026 class has shown why already, proving why he could be the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NBA Draft. He's been averaging 14.8 points with a team-high eight rebounds per game. His ability to impact the game has boosted the Jayhawks' productivity on the court with one of the top offensives in the country.

Winning the Players Era would be a strong resume builder for Kansas, which has started the season 5-0 with a win against Kentucky already on the resume. It could also propel the No. 9 Jayhawks to the top of the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll after the top four teams in the rankings all lost this week, and beating the No. 7 Cougars that took down No. 1 Florida would make it half of the top 10 going down.

articles.title: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld's 7-month-old daughter Harper gets her first Hollywood debut
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld and Josh Allen's little girl is already making her mark in Hollywood, and she hasn't even celebrated her first birthday yet!
articles.body: Hailee Steinfeld and Josh Allen's little girl is already making her mark in Hollywood, and she hasn't even celebrated her first birthday yet! The actress recently revealed a sweet surprise about her seven-month-old daughter, Harper Haize Allen, who has officially received her first movie credit in Disney's upcoming animated film Hexed.Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld's daughter Harper lands her first movie credit before her first birthday in adorable Disney traditionSteinfeld shared the adorable detail in her Beau Society newsletter, revealing that Harper's name appears in the movie's end credits. While the little one obviously hasn't made her acting debut (technically) just yet, she has already secured a special place in the Disney production.And there's actually a very sweet reason behind it!Harper's appearance in the credits is part of a long-running tradition in the animation industry. Disney and Pixar productions have been known to include the names of babies born to cast and crew members while a movie is being made.Often referred to as "Production Babies," these special mentions are a way of celebrating the little ones who arrive while their parents are busy bringing an animated film to life. The tradition has become a beloved little detail for animation fans, with parents getting to see their children's names preserved in the closing credits of a movie they helped create.For Harper, that means her first Hollywood credit comes courtesy of her mother's latest project, even before she is old enough to understand what a movie credit actually means!Hailee Steinfeld's Disney project gets an extra-special connectionSteinfeld voices Billie Doe in Disney's upcoming animated movie Hexed, which is scheduled to arrive in theaters on November 25, 2026. The project already holds a special place in the actress's career, but Harper's inclusion gives it an even more personal connection. Instead of simply watching her mother's name appear on the big screen, Hailee will also get to see her daughter's name among the people being celebrated in the credits.Steinfeld and Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen welcomed Harper in 2026, and the couple have been enjoying their new chapter as parents. Now, while Allen continues to make headlines on the football field, his little girl has secured her own tiny Hollywood milestone. articles.title: Adam Schefter Predicts 'Auction' to Trade Up for Drew Mestemaker at No. 1 in 2027 NFL Draft
articles.summary: Several teams could try to trade up and select Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
Several teams could try to trade up and select Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft.

ESPN's Adam Schefter predicted that front offices will attempt to trade for the No. 1 choice in order to add Mestemaker if the Tennessee Titans or Los Angeles Chargers finish with the worst record in the NFL.

"If the Titans or the Chargers with the number one pick, there is going to be an auction, I believe, for the number one pick for the right to go draft Drew Mestemaker," Schefter said during Thursday's episode of the Adam Schefter Podcast (0:27 mark). "The Oklahoma State quarterback. Whether that's the Jets trading up, whether that's the Cardinals trading up, whether that's any of these other teams."

"Somebody's gonna want to trade up to number one if it's Tennessee or the Chargers," he added.

After Mestemaker helped North Texas compile the No. 1 scoring offense in the country during the 2025 season, he's spearheaded a Cowboys offense that ranks No. 3 in the nation by averaging 42.2 points per game this year.

In 10 appearances, he's completed 66.4 percent of his throws for 3,239 yards and 30 touchdowns as well as 10 interceptions. He's also rushed for 169 yards and four scores.

Mestemaker was projected to be selected with the No. 3 overall pick in the latest mock draft from Bleacher Report's NFL Scouting Department.

The Titans and Chargers have both struggled this year, but they might not be searching for a new quarterback near the top of the draft.

Tennessee's Cam Ward has dealt with some inconsistency throughout his budding career, but the No. 1 overall choice in the 2025 draft is still just 24 years old and has shown promise of late.

After all, the two-time Pro Bowler racked up 7,597 pass yards to go along with 49 touchdowns and 16 interceptions across 33 starts from 2024-25.

articles.title: Rams star Puka Nacua suspended 3 games by NFL for conduct violations
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy, and he will serve the ban while already on injured reserve.
articles.body: Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy, and he will serve the ban while already on injured reserve. The All-Pro receiver won’t be paid during his suspension, the league announced. But thanks to the timing of his ban, Nacua won’t miss any games that he wouldn’t already miss because of his sprained knee ligaments and turf toe. Nacua went on injured reserve last week, and he is eligible to return both from IR and his suspension when the Rams (6-4) host the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 20. The Rams and Nacua have been awaiting his probable suspension for nearly a year, and it was finally announced during their bye week. The NFL said it doesn’t consider a player’s injury status when announcing discipline at the close of an investigation, and Nacua joins a handful of players who have received disciplinary suspensions in recent years while they were also unable to play for other reasons. Nacua apologized last December for performing a gesture that plays upon antisemitic tropes during an internet livestream, claiming he didn’t understand what it meant. Nacua was then sued in March by a woman who claims he bit her on the arm and made an antisemitic statement during a night of partying on New Year’s Eve. Nacua briefly entered a holistic rehabilitation facility during the offseason, and he told an interviewer before the Rams’ season opener that he had misused alcohol in the past. The scandals colored the rapid rise to stardom for a former fifth-round pick who has been one of the most productive receivers in NFL history over his first four seasons. Nacua set the NFL record for yards receiving by a rookie in 2023, and he led the league in receptions last season while earning his first All-Pro nod. He has 383 catches for 4,906 yards and 23 touchdowns in just 51 games, with another 44 catches for 654 yards in six playoff games. Nacua is eligible for a hefty contract extension now, but he has played in just seven games during the final year of his rookie contract. He has made 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns this season, but Nacua also missed two games with a core muscle injury in September before hurting his knee on the final offensive play of the Rams’ win at Washington on Nov. 8. Despite the injury absences of starting receivers Nacua and Davante Adams, the Rams are on a four-game winning streak. They return from their bye to host the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Explains How He's 'Simplified Life' Since Trade to Vikings from Raiders at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The past week has been a whirlwind for Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins, but the veteran has kept his poise by relying on the words of Mark Dantonio, his college coach at Michigan State.
articles.body:
The past week has been a whirlwind for Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins, but the veteran has kept his poise by relying on the words of Mark Dantonio, his college coach at Michigan State.

"Mark Dantonio would always say that when things speed up, he would always try to slow down," Cousins said Thursday, per ESPN's Kevin Seifert . "And that's always stuck with me whenever life starts to get busy, is to actually try to go the opposite direction and slow down. So I've really simplified life. I've got about 150 text messages I haven't responded to. My wife is handling a lot of things and I'm pretty much just really basic, just coming to work and going home, and life's actually been really slow and boring in a way by design. So there's a lot of things going on maybe outside, but I kind of have 'ignorance is bliss' and just focus on football."

The Las Vegas Raiders traded Cousins to the Vikings for a third-round pick ahead of the NFL's trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 18. After just four full days with the team, Cousins led the Vikings' offense to its most productive outing of the 2026 season in Sunday's 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers.

In the matter of one week, Cousins had to play a road game in San Francisco, travel back to Las Vegas, say his goodbyes to former teammates, move to Minnesota, meet his new teammates, and start a road game against a divisional rival in Lambeau Field — the same stadium where he suffered the worst injury of his career.

Cousins became the first quarterback in NFL history to start for two different teams in back-to-back weeks, per Seifert.

The whirlwind readjustment will continue this week as the Vikings prepare for an international game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City.

Cousins lost to the 49ers in his last game with Las Vegas, but this time he'll be accompanied by the league's No. 1 scoring defense rather than the Raiders' defense, which has allowed the second-most points among all teams.

articles.title: The father behind the champion: How Pat Mahomes Sr.’s love, sacrifices and life lessons shaped Patrick Mahomes’ NFL journey and helped hold their father-son bond strong
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has become one of the biggest names in the NFL, known for his ability to stay calm, make difficult throws and lead the Kansas City Chiefs
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has become one of the biggest names in the NFL, known for his ability to stay calm, make difficult throws and lead the Kansas City Chiefs through high-pressure moments. But behind the quarterback’s success is a father who helped him understand what it takes to compete at the highest level. Pat Mahomes Sr., a former Major League Baseball pitcher, gave Patrick more than an early love for sports. He taught him to work hard, move on from mistakes and believe in his own choices, lessons that have stayed with him throughout his football career.Pat Mahomes Sr. introduced Patrick Mahomes to the world of professional sportsPatrick’s connection with sports began when he was very young. His father played professional baseball, so trips to the ballpark became a regular part of his childhood. Pat Sr. pitched in Major League Baseball from 1992 to 2003, representing teams such as the Minnesota Twins, Boston Red Sox, New York Mets, Texas Rangers, Chicago Cubs and Pittsburgh Pirates.For Patrick, those visits were about much more than watching a game. He got to see what life looked like for professional athletes before he was old enough to understand all the hard work behind it. He wore team uniforms, spent time around the players and watched his father prepare for games. One of his early memories was catching a ball during batting practice when he was around five years old.Growing up around baseball also meant Patrick saw the less glamorous side of being a professional athlete. He watched his father travel, train, compete and deal with the pressure that came with every game. Pat Sr. had worked hard to reach the highest level of baseball, and his son had a chance to see that effort up close.Patrick later spoke about watching his father fight for his place in the sport. Seeing him keep working towards his goals helped Patrick understand that talent alone is not enough. An athlete has to be ready when an opportunity arrives because there is no guarantee that the same chance will come again.Those early years gave Patrick a close look at professional sports, but the most important lessons came from the conversations he had with his father.Pat Mahomes Sr. taught Patrick Mahomes how to handle pressure and failureBeing a professional pitcher is not easy. A single poor throw can change an inning, and a mistake can quickly put a team in a difficult position. Pat Sr. understood that feeling well, and he wanted his son to learn how to deal with it rather than allow one bad moment to affect everything that followed.He shared a simple lesson with Patrick: “It’s always about the next play. It’s always about the next pitch.”The message was clear. An athlete cannot go back and change a mistake, but he can decide how he responds to it. Instead of thinking about a missed opportunity, he must focus on what comes next.That advice became especially useful when Patrick moved into football. A quarterback faces difficult situations almost every week. He may throw an interception, miss an open receiver or lose an important game, but he cannot afford to let frustration take control. His teammates still look to him for direction, and he has to be ready for the next play.Patrick’s calm approach in difficult moments reflects the lessons he learned while watching his father play baseball. His ability to reset after a mistake has become an important part of his game, especially during close playoff contests and Super Bowl appearances.Pat Sr. did not teach his son that he would never fail. Instead, he showed him that failure is part of sports and that an athlete’s response matters just as much as the result. It was a lesson Patrick could carry with him whether he was playing in college or leading an NFL team.Pat Mahomes Sr. supported Patrick Mahomes when he chose football over baseballWith a father who had spent more than a decade in Major League Baseball, it would have been easy to expect Patrick to follow the same path. He was also a talented baseball player and even had an opportunity to enter the sport professionally after being selected by the Detroit Tigers in the 2014 MLB Draft.However, Patrick had another dream. He wanted to play football, and his father allowed him to make that decision without putting pressure on him to become a baseball player.Pat Sr. understood that his son’s future had to be based on what Patrick wanted, not on what he had achieved himself. When Patrick committed to football, he knew his father would support him.Patrick once spoke about that support and said, “I always had his full support.” He also explained that his father understood how much football meant to him and wanted him to follow the sport he loved.That kind of support mattered because choosing football meant taking a different road. Patrick had to prove himself at Texas Tech before entering the NFL Draft, and there was no guarantee that he would become the player he is today. His father could offer advice from his own experience, but Patrick had to build his career through his own performances.Pat Sr. also made it clear that he did not expect his son to be perfect. He wanted him to give his best effort, stay positive and keep working, even when things did not go as planned.For Patrick, having that freedom meant he could make his own decisions without feeling that he had to live up to his father’s baseball career. He was allowed to build a name for himself in a different sport, while still learning from the person who knew professional competition better than most.Pat Mahomes Sr. remained beside Patrick Mahomes through success and difficult timesPatrick’s rise in the NFL did not change the importance of his father in his life. Pat Sr. continued to attend games, celebrate major achievements and support his son as he became one of football’s leading quarterbacks. For a parent who had watched his child grow up around professional sports, seeing those dreams turn into reality was a special experience.Patrick has spoken about how much his father means to him. In an interview with CNN, he said, “My dad, he means the world to me, man. I mean, he set an example for me on how you have to go through this business.” He also spoke about watching his father work through difficult years in baseball and how those experiences shaped his own approach to sport.Their relationship has also faced difficult moments. In 2024, Pat Sr. was arrested on a driving while intoxicated charge. Patrick later spoke about the situation and the effect it had on his family. It was a painful personal matter, but it also showed that their relationship was not free from challenges. Like many families, they have had to deal with difficult situations while trying to support one another.The bond between Patrick and his father is not only about football or baseball. It is also about a parent giving his child the freedom to choose a future, offering advice without taking control and remaining present as life changes.Patrick Mahomes has built his NFL career through his own talent, effort and decisions. His father cannot take credit for the passes he throws or the games he wins. But Pat Sr. played an important role long before the world began watching Patrick. He gave his son an early understanding of hard work, taught him how to respond to pressure and stood behind him when he chose a different path. Those lessons became part of the person and player Patrick is today.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jordon Hudson’s ‘Gold Digger’ trademark application challenged by California pawn shop after 18 years
articles.summary: Jordon Hudson is facing a trademark challenge after a California pawn shop asked the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) to block her
articles.body: Jordon Hudson is facing a trademark challenge after a California pawn shop asked the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) to block her company’s application for the name “Gold Digger.” The 25-year-old filed the request in August 2025 through TCE Rights Management LLC, seeking to use the name for jewelry and key chains. The shop, also called The Gold Digger, says it has used the name since February 2008. It filed its formal opposition on November 16, 2026. The USPTO case is now pending, and no decision has yet been made in the dispute.The Gold Digger Pawn Shop Challenges Jordon Hudson's Trademark Application Filed Through TCE Rights ManagementThe dispute involves two businesses seeking rights to a similar name. Hudson's company filed its application on August 25, 2025. According to the trademark filing, the planned products include jewelry and key chains under the Gold Digger name.The California business is based in Elk Grove, just south of Sacramento. It says it has been using The Gold Digger name since February 1, 2008. Its website also states that the pawn shop was established in 1968.The shop took its complaint to the USPTO after Hudson's application moved forward in the registration process. The application was approved for publication in April 2026 and appeared in the official publication for trademark applications in May.The Gold Digger first requested more time to challenge the application in June. It later received further extensions before submitting its formal opposition on November 16.The case is listed on the USPTO's Trademark Trial and Appeal Board website. TCE Rights Management LLC is named as the defendant, while The Gold Digger is listed as the party challenging the application. The case remains open.According to ESPN, the law office representing the pawn shop declined to comment when contacted about the matter. PEOPLE also reported that Hudson had not publicly commented on the challenge.Jordon Hudson's Business Links to Bill Belichick Continue Despite Reported SplitThe trademark dispute has also brought attention to Hudson's other business activities involving Bill Belichick. The 25-year-old has been closely linked to the 74-year-old football coach, who now leads the University of North Carolina football team.A November 11 report by the Daily Mail said Hudson was still managing 18 companies connected to Belichick, despite reports that the pair had ended their relationship nearly a year earlier.According to Massachusetts state records cited by the publication, Hudson filed annual reports for 14 of those companies in July. She also made changes to four businesses linked to the Belichick brand. One of them handles his trademarks.TCE Rights Management is among the companies involved in these business activities. It was set up to handle intellectual property, including trademarks and copyrights.The company has also tried to secure names linked to Belichick's football career. These include "Chapel Bill," "Chapel Bill (Bill's Version)," "All-Belichick Team" and "All-Time Belichick Team."However, not every application received approval. ESPN reported that four earlier trademark requests were rejected in September 2025. They included "Do Your Job (Bill's Version)," "Ignore the Noise (Bill's Version)," "The Belestrator (Bill's Version)" and "No Days Off (Bill's Version)."The New England Patriots already held trademarks for similar phrases. The USPTO refused the applications over concerns that the names could confuse customers.The latest challenge is separate from those earlier refusals. The Gold Digger pawn shop is now asking the trademark board to stop Hudson's company from securing the name. The board has not announced an outcome, so the application remains tied up in the opposition process.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mexico City’s high-profile showdown and ‘Byemaggedon’ highlights Week 11 in the NFL
articles.summary: This weekend brings a heavyweight NFL showdown in Mexico City, a nightmare for fantasy football owners and some of the biggest betting spreads we’ve seen in years.
articles.body: With the NFL playoff picture beginning to take shape, Week 11 brings a heavyweight showdown in Mexico City, a nightmare for fantasy football owners and some of the biggest betting spreads we’ve seen in years. Meanwhile, Joe Burrow is making a serious push for the season’s MVP and the injury-ravaged Lions say it’s next man up. Here are 5 things to know about Week 11. Sunday night in CDMX The NFL’s international slate wraps up Sunday, but don’t worry about setting an early alarm. The Vikings (7-2) and 49ers (8-1) will square off in primetime at Estadio Banorte (formerly called the Estadio Azteca) in Mexico City, marking the league’s sixth game in Mexico. And both teams are going to extreme lengths to prepare for the altitude. San Francisco spent the week training at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, while Minnesota took a more high-tech approach, constructing a “high-altitude room” at its facility that simulates elevations up to 12,000 feet. Vikings players have logged nearly 450 sessions in the chamber over the past five weeks. Kyle Shanahan already won one international preparation battle this season, arriving early in Australia before the 49ers hammered the Rams 27-7 in the opener. Will his strategy pay off again? On the field, it’s a fascinating clash of strengths: Brian Flores’ defense ranks second in yards allowed, while the 49ers boast the NFL’s top-ranked offense. And with Kirk Cousins back under center, Minnesota has renewed confidence in its passing game. Cousins could become the first quarterback to lead two different teams in touchdown passes in the same season. He threw 20 with the Raiders before returning to Minnesota, where he’s just four touchdowns away from overtaking Kyler Murray for the Vikings’ team lead. “Byemaggedon” has arrived Fantasy football owners, good luck setting your lineups this week. The dreaded “Byemaggedon” is here, with a season-high six teams taking the week off. The Falcons, Browns, Packers, Rams, Patriots and Seahawks can all rest up for Week 12. That means plenty of fantasy stars will be unavailable at a critical point in the season, just as leagues enter the home stretch before the playoffs. The NFL traditionally loads up on byes before Thanksgiving, when the schedule gets even more complicated. No teams will be off during Thanksgiving week, but the byes return in Week 13 with the Colts, Raiders, Giants and Ravens resting. The Cowboys and Cardinals will finally get their turn in Week 14. Massive spreads, upsets to come? Oddsmakers aren’t expecting much drama in several Week 11 matchups. A whopping five teams are favored by double digits, which, according to Action Network, would be the most such games through the first 11 weeks of an NFL season since 2009. The Bills are 16.5-point favorites over the Dolphins, the Chiefs are laying 15.5, the Texans are favored by 12.5 over the Colts, the Bears are giving 11.5 and the Broncos are 10-point favorites over the Raiders. But don’t pencil in those wins just yet. We’ve already seen two double-digit underdogs pull off outright upsets this season. The Cardinals stunned the Rams in Week 6 as 12.5-point underdogs, and the Giants knocked off the Texans in Week 7 despite entering as 10-point dogs. With five opportunities for another massive upset, don’t be surprised if at least one favorite gets a rude awakening Sunday. Burrow’s MVP march heads to DC Can anyone slow down Joe Burrow right now? The Bengals quarterback has been absolutely surgical during Cincinnati’s five-game winning streak, throwing an eye-popping 20 touchdowns against just three interceptions. After knocking off the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, Burrow and the Bengals are back in primetime for the second straight week, this time facing Dan Quinn’s Commanders on Monday night. Burrow has surged to the front of the MVP conversation, and his numbers are approaching historic territory. He’s on pace for 51 touchdown passes, a total that would trail only Peyton Manning’s record-setting 55 in 2013. The Bengals are rolling, Burrow is playing arguably the best football of his career, and another national television showcase gives him a chance to strengthen his MVP case. Lions remain steadfast despite pain The Lions just can’t catch a break. Detroit’s injury nightmare took another devastating turn last week when star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye. To make matters worse, Maye suffered a severe ankle injury on the same play. Asked whether he would consider banning celebrations, Dan Campbell delivered a classic response: “We’re not talking to 8-year-olds here.” But the injury has certainly gotten players’ attention around the league. Giants running back Cam Skattebo says he’s retiring his signature touchdown backflip after seeing what happened to Hutchinson. For Detroit, the bigger concern is what happens next. The Lions had already lost standout linebacker Jack Campbell to a serious neck injury, leaving them without arguably their two most important defensive players. That puts even more pressure on Detroit’s explosive offense to carry the load down the stretch. The Lions host the Buccaneers on Sunday. articles.body: Clyde Edwards-Helaire had more than a football career to consider when he entered the 2024 NFL free agency market.
