In 2024, Edwards-Helaire openly discussed how the veteran tight end supported him during the toughest periods of his career."Personal level, from football to on a day-to-day basis, he's someone that's been in my corner and picked me up from my lowest of lows," Edwards-Helaire said of Kelce. "And then when I was on my highest of highs, just being there, trying to put a rocket on my back. So you just have that camaraderie."His comments offered a glimpse into the culture that helped Kansas City retain players. Kelce's influence was not limited to his performances on the field. articles.title: Caleb Williams, Josh Allen, JSN Headline Top-Selling NFL Jerseys During 2026 Season
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams needed just two and a half seasons to become the most popular jersey in the NFL.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams needed just two and a half seasons to become the most popular jersey in the NFL.

According to Fanatics , Williams had the top-selling jersey for the first half of the season, followed by Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen, Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love and San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner.

Others cracking the top-10 include Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson, 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy and Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb.

It's not much of a surprise to see Williams so high on the list. For one, he plays in a big market and is a young player, so many fans are buying his jersey for the first time this year.

He's also lived up to the hype that came with him being drafted No. 1 overall in 2024. Despite dealing with a hamstring injury earlier this year, he's thrown for 1,546 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions in six games, leading the Bears to a 7-2 start.

Allen is a household name at this point, but he's seemingly only getting more popular, considering his jersey was one of the highest-selling during the first half of the season.

Smith-Njigba perhaps established himself as the best receiver in the NFL last season, and he's been dominant once again this year, leading the league in receptions (79), yards (1,207) and touchdowns (10).

Love has put together a fantastic season so far, leading the league with 2,838 passing yards, 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. The Packers have a massive fan base despite being in a smaller market, so it's no surprise to see his jersey be such a popular one.

Warner was the only defensive player to crack the list, and that perhaps speaks to how beloved the veteran is in both San Francisco and around the country. The 30-year-old is a four-time first-team All-Pro member and has managed to stay productive as he's gotten older.

articles.title: Is GTA 6 really distracting NFL players? Browns quarterback drops surprising admission as playoff hopes grow

articles.body: The Cleveland Browns had unexpectedly put themselves in the AFC playoff conversation, but their players appeared to have something very different on their minds. With a winning record and a wild-card position to protect, Deshaun Watson was asked whether the team had started discussing its postseason chances. His response caught attention for an entirely different reason. The Browns entered their bye week with a 6-4 record, holding the AFC's third wild-card position and seventh seed. He told the Associated Press that he had preordered the game for its midnight release and “told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days.”Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila even joked about how the release could affect players' recovery routines. “If you could check guys' sleep scores ... I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down,” he told the AP.For Cleveland, however, the break would not last forever. articles.title: Bears' Stadium Decision Timeline Updated in New NFL Rumors with Illinois Vote Looming
articles.summary: Chicago Bears chairman George McCaskey and president Kevin Warren spoke with the NFL's stadium committee during league meetings in New York on Thursday regarding the team's potential future stadium homes in Illinois and Indiana, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears chairman George McCaskey and president Kevin Warren spoke with the NFL's stadium committee during league meetings in New York on Thursday regarding the team's potential future stadium homes in Illinois and Indiana, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.

Progress on the stadium front was "well-received" by the committee, per Rapoport. However, the reporter noted that the clock is ticking in Illinois because the state's General Assembly's final 2026 veto session ends on Dec. 3.

The key question here is why Dec. 3 is considered the "deadline" of sorts. Marc Ganis, president of Sports Corp Limited, explained why to Craig Wall of ABC7 Chicago.

Ideal Offseason Landing Spots for NFL QB Reclamation Projects 🛬

"The reality is the end of the fall veto session, which is Dec. 3, has to be the deadline, because if you allow it to go into the next legislative session, as we all know in Illinois, nothing gets done until the last week of May," he said. "And there is no expectation that Indiana is going to wait around another six months."

Indiana has already approved the groundwork for a stadium to be built in Hammond, which is roughly 25 miles from the Loop in Chicago.

Last February, the state's House Ways and Means Committee unanimously approved an amendment by a 24-0 vote to Indiana State Bill 27 to get it done.

Last June , the Bears' board of directors voted to advance the stadium project in the state.

However, as the calendar inches closer to November, nothing has been finalized on that front.

Dan Wiederer and Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic provided more insight into the "best-case scenario" for the Bears remaining in Illinois.

"In the best-case scenario for the Bears, with three days of governing sessions this week plus three more Dec. 1-3, the state Senate and House of Representatives will push forward a bill that provides the team a framework for tax certainty and requested infrastructure aid to resume seriously pursuing its stadium project in Illinois.

"The Bears' desired project location in Illinois remains Arlington Heights, where the organization owns 326 acres of property on a site that has been pad-ready for some time and offers substantial space for both a stadium and a mixed-use development and entertainment district.

"Will this stadium venture finally move ahead in Illinois? We'll see. Shovels in the ground in 2027? Perhaps. But it's worth emphasizing that this saga remains fluid — and has been for years."

At this juncture, Arlington Heights, Illinois and Hammond, Indiana seem like the two clear leaders in the clubhouse.

However, there's also a $10 billion plan via Capri Investment Group and GRIT Chicago that would keep the Bears in town create a stadium and an entertainment district on the former Michael Reese Hospital site, per Shelby Hawkins of WTTW (Chicago's PBS station). The hospital was located in he Bronzeville neighborhood (Near South Side).

Ultimately, Dec. 3 seems like the date to watch at this juncture, and one can surmise fans and onlookers might get more clarity on the situation soon enough.

articles.summary: A 4-11 skid leaves the human searching for answers, while ChatGPT enters NFL Week 11 with two straight winning cards and a chance to erase a shrinking deficit.
articles.body: If I wasn’t officially ice cold entering Week 10, I certainly am entering Week 11. After another losing week (2-3, -1.33 units), I am now 4-11 and down 8.52 units since the start of Week 8. But there is good news. As someone who publicly posts betting picks on the internet, I’ve often said that you either need to be really good or really bad. If you’re really good, people can follow your picks and make money. If you’re really bad, people can fade your picks and make money. If you’re just average, then you basically just lose the juice and cost everyone money. That’s the worst-case scenario. ONE WILD WEEK 11 BETTING STAT SHOWS JUST HOW FAR APART THE NFL’S BEST AND WORST TEAMS ARE Right now, I might be one of the best on the internet at providing fadable NFL picks. And that’s something. It’s not great for me. But it’s good for you. And my No. 1 priority is the audience, so you know what? It’s good for me, too. Both of us get five selections from the same odds board, with no bet priced worse than -120. Odds were taken from the board supplied Thursday at 4 p.m. ET. Stakes are adjusted so every winning bet produces one unit of profit. For example, -110 requires risking 1.10 units, while +110 requires approximately 0.91 units. A push returns the stake and counts as zero units. Week 10 NFL Betting Results Dan’s Week 10 NFL Betting Picks (2-3, -1.33 units) Washington won outright on Thursday Night Football, and the Dolphins-Colts over got us another winner. I thought I was headed toward a winning week, but Drake Maye suffered a potentially season-ending ankle injury in the first quarter against Detroit (not the first time a team we bet on lost its quarterback in the first 15 minutes of a game). Then, the Texans had a 17-0 lead and blew it against the CLEVELAND BROWNS. That pretty much sums up my season. Actually, the Steelers falling into a 31-3 hole against the Bengals probably sums it up better. WHICH NFL TEAMS CAN ACTUALLY WIN THE SUPER BOWL? RANKING ALL 32 AT THE SEASON’S HALFWAY POINT GPT’s Week 10 NFL Betting Picks (3-2, +0.77 units) GPT went 3-2 for the second straight week and picked up another 0.77 units. The Chiefs and Bills covered comfortably, while the Vikings and Packers stayed under the total. The 49ers and Cowboys combined for 86 points, so that was a bad miss. Then it joined me on Pittsburgh. I was right about one thing: "Theoretically, I should be more confident now, but suddenly I'm worried. That can't be good, right?" That's what I wrote when GPT spit out the same Pittsburgh pick that I had. I guess I was right that I was probably going to be wrong. Season report card DAN: 23-26-1, -5.32 units GPT: 22-27-1, -6.90 units I still lead GPT by 1.58 units, although bragging about losing less money than a robot probably tells you everything you need to know about how this season is going. Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week: 6-3, +2.83 units At least the Plug Your Nose bet is making money. Maybe the problem is that I’m only picking one of those per week. Dan’s Week 11 NFL Betting Card 1. Tennessee Titans +8 (-108) Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: Nothing says "let’s turn this season around" like betting on the Tennessee Titans. But this is the kind of ugly underdog I want to be backing. Tennessee has scored at least 23 points in four straight games, while Dallas ranks last in yards allowed and 30th in scoring defense. Changing the defensive play-caller to Mike Pettine shows how desperate the Cowboys are to adjust, but Pettine doesn't magically help the personnel get better. That makes Tennessee this week’s Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week. The name continues to do a lot of work. GPT’s analysis: We’re on the same side. Tennessee has scored at least 23 points in four straight games, and Dallas allows a league-worst 154.1 rushing yards per game. I paid for +9½ because the Titans can lose 31-23 and still cash. That score pushes your bet, but I like getting better than a touchdown at -108. 2. Pittsburgh Steelers -4½ (-110) Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: The Steelers embarrassed us on Sunday Night Football, and now I’m laying points with them on the road. Apparently, I just hate myself. But getting blown out by Cincinnati doesn’t suddenly make Pittsburgh a bad team. The Steelers are still 6-3, while Philadelphia is 2-7 and starting Joe Milton III for the second time. I think Pittsburgh’s pass rush can make life difficult for an inexperienced quarterback and create the kind of mistakes that help a road favorite cover. I expect T.J. Watt and company to want to make a statement after the embarrassment on Sunday Night Football. NFL WEEK 10 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS LOOK UNBEATABLE, CHIEFS ARE SCARY AGAIN, DEMECO RYANS IS ON THE HOT SEAT GPT’s analysis: Pittsburgh was the first side I left off my card. Joe Milton took seven sacks against the Giants, and the Steelers allow just 83.2 rushing yards per game. Philadelphia may have to let him throw. My concern is Pittsburgh averaging only 1.55 points per road drive. I’d pay five cents more for -4 in case this ends 20-16. 3. New York Jets-Los Angeles Chargers Under 41½ (-105) New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: Of course the Chargers finally won when I stopped betting on them. Another symbol of just how this season has gone. But one win doesn’t convince me that this offense is fixed, especially since it gained less than 300 yards against the Ravens. Los Angeles still averages just 16 points per game, while the Jets average 19.4. The Chargers are also returning from a Monday night game in Baltimore, leaving them a shorter week to prepare. Neither defense is airtight, and a couple of turnovers that hand the opponent a short field could ruin this. Still, I’m expecting more stalled drives than fireworks because neither team is great at forcing turnovers (Jets have 12 takeaways this season and the Chargers have 14). GPT’s analysis: This was my favorite game to bet under. The Jets have gone two full games without a touchdown, and the Chargers just won with Justin Herbert throwing for 129 yards. I’d still take 41½ at -105. I prefer 42 at -108 because those extra three cents get my money back if this finishes 23-19. 4. Minnesota Vikings +3½ (-120) Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers, Sunday Night Football in Mexico City Dan’s analysis: San Francisco just scored 46 points against Dallas, but I’m not treating the Cowboys’ defense as a preview of this matchup. Minnesota allows the fewest points per drive in the NFL and ranks second in defensive EPA per play. This defense can make the 49ers work for their points, and I expect them to do just that. Kirk Cousins immediately improved the Vikings’ offense, and I think Kirko Chainz can keep this within a field goal on Monday Night Football in Mexico City (just don’t look up Cousins’ record in primetime). GPT’s analysis: Minnesota allows 14 points per game, and a 23-20 loss in Mexico City would cash this ticket. My hesitation is San Francisco’s offense, which leads the NFL in points per drive and offensive EPA per play. That kept me off the Vikings at -120. 5. Washington Commanders +6½ (-108) Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders, Monday Night Football Dan’s analysis: Yes, I’m fading the Bengals again even though I couldn’t have been more wrong with my approach last week against Pittsburgh. This game perfectly fits my NFL betting approach: Cincinnati looked terrific in a standalone game, and now I’m getting nearly a touchdown with a home underdog that has extra rest after playing on Thursday Night Football. Plus, I’m a Jayden Daniels truther. GPT’s analysis: Jayden Daniels’ legs give Washington a way to keep this close, especially with the extra rest after Thursday Night Football. I took Cincinnati because Washington blitzes on 42.1% of dropbacks and Joe Burrow completes 73.4% against the blitz. We can both win this one, though. Bengals 27, Commanders 21 would do it. Also explain exactly why you’re passing on the eligible bets you don’t select. Use at least 10 different sources for each game so you have a broad understanding of everything surrounding each game. Before delivering the results, do a fact-check and ensure that everything is correct." After 10 minutes of thinking, here is what it came up with: 1. Tampa Bay Buccaneers-Detroit Lions Under 45½ (-104) Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET GPT’s analysis: Jahmyr Gibbs just put up 252 yards from scrimmage in Munich. Tampa Bay gives him a tougher draw. The Bucs have held opposing teams below 100 rushing yards in eight straight games, and they lead the league in rushing yards per game themselves. Tampa can take time off the clock and make Detroit do the same. Detroit has allowed 14.4 points per game during its five-game winning streak. Tampa Bay fails to pick up a first down on 37.1% of its possessions. Even if Baker Mayfield plays, the Lions can win 27-17 and there’s still room under 45½. GPT’s projected score: Lions 24, Buccaneers 17 Dan’s analysis: Both teams like to run the ball, so I can see this staying under. But the Lions' defense has taken a big hit in recent weeks, losing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson and the Bucs can score if Baker Mayfield plays. I'd probably avoid this total. 2. Tennessee Titans +9½ (-120) Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET GPT’s analysis: Tennessee has scored at least 23 points in four straight games since picking up the tempo on offense. Dallas just gave up 584 yards to San Francisco and changed defensive play callers. Mike Pettine’s first assignment is fixing a run defense that allows a league-worst 154.1 yards per game. Dak Prescott could have another big day against a defense that’s allowed 40 or more in back-to-back games. At +7½, a late Dallas field goal that stretches a six-point lead to nine beats me. At +9½, I can live with it. GPT’s projected score: Cowboys 31, Titans 24 Dan’s analysis: I'm also on Tennessee, but I elected to take fewer points with less juice. Still, I obviously favor siding with the Titans this week. 3. New York Jets-Los Angeles Chargers Under 42 (-108) New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET GPT’s analysis: The Jets got all 24 of their points against the Chiefs and Bills from eight field goals. The Chargers finally won in Baltimore with Justin Herbert throwing for just 129 yards. They ran for 160, and they have every reason to give the ball to Omarion Hampton again against a Jets defense allowing 135.3 rushing yards per game. The last five Jets games all cleared 42, but Kansas City and Buffalo scored 35 and 31 to get the last two there. The Chargers average 16. I’ll take the under. GPT’s projected score: Chargers 20, Jets 16 Dan’s analysis: Well, GPT and I are finding a lot of common ground this week. That's probably bad news for the robot. Sorry, buddy. 4. Jacksonville Jaguars -5½ (-115) Jacksonville Jaguars at New York Giants, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET GPT’s analysis: Jacksonville has scored at least 30 points in four straight games, and the defense allows just 16 per game. That gives Trevor Lawrence some room for an ordinary afternoon. If Jacksonville scores 24, the Giants need at least 19 against the NFL’s second-ranked scoring defense to cover. The Giants force a three-and-out on a third of their opponents’ drives, and Jacksonville is starting backup center Jonah Monheim. That’s why I want -5½. If New York forces Lawrence to settle for a late field goal and Jacksonville wins 23-17, I still cash. GPT’s projected score: Jaguars 27, Giants 20 Dan’s analysis: I looked at the Giants but couldn't pull the trigger. The Jags have done a good job this season of beating up on bad teams and, yes, the Giants are a bad team. I'm not sold on Jacksonville overall, but I couldn't get there with the Giants in Week 11. 5. Cincinnati Bengals -5½ (-115) Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders, Monday Night Football GPT’s analysis: Washington sends extra rushers on 42.1% of dropbacks. The Commanders have allowed touchdowns on 23 of 32 red-zone trips, and Cincinnati has scored at least 31 points in five straight wins. Jayden Daniels’ legs and the extra rest after Thursday Night Football give Washington a chance to hang around. I’ll pay -115 for the half-point so a 27-21 Bengals win still cashes. articles.title: 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk reveals hardest part of playing in Mexico City as San Fran returns to face Vikings
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers trained at the Air Force Academy to adapt to Mexico City's thin air before facing the Minnesota Vikings on "Sunday Night Football."
articles.body: Earlier this season, the San Francisco 49ers seemed to gain an edge in their game-week prep by flying down to Australia while the Los Angeles Rams stayed home. In Week 11, as the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings head down to Mexico City for yet another NFL international matchup, they are hoping for an edge to prepare for a different challenge this time. It isn’t a time difference, but rather a massive elevation difference in Mexico City. The capital of Mexico sits 7,350 feet above sea level, which is roughly 2,000 feet higher than Denver, Colorado, known as the Mile High City. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE So, the 49ers have been preparing for this week against a tough Minnesota opponent at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs to get acclimated to the thin air. Fullback Kyle Juszczyk, who was a member of the 49ers when they thrashed the Arizona Cardinals four years ago in Mexico City, believes his team’s strategy is sound considering his experience. "I think just being here a week early is going to help a lot," he told OutKick during a recent interview. "Just training in it, sleeping in it — just being in it for a week. Definitely gives you at least an opportunity to feel what that feels like and let your body adapt. We did the same thing, I think it was four years ago, when we played in Mexico City. We had a good result. We won the game pretty big against Arizona. So, hoping for the same thing this week." Juszczyk knows, though, that Mexico City’s air is going to be a struggle even with the training. "The hardest thing was getting back into the locker room. We went down, we did our warm-ups. Felt pretty good, but the stadium in Mexico City I just remember to get back to our locker room was a long walk and the incline was like 45 degrees. articles.body:
Sam Hartman is trading football for reality TV as the Washington Commanders quarterback is set to be the star of the new season of ABC's The Bachelor .

Hartman spoke about his decision to go on the show, and he revealed that he's never actually seen it before.

"I haven't seen an episode, so if you guys have any tips I would love to hear your thoughts on the dos and do nots," Hartman said. "But I'm gonna probably do some tape watching after the season's over and study up."

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase Eyes NFL History With Tee Higgins Amid Bengals WRs' Strong Seasons
articles.summary: Ja'Marr Chase has lofty goals for himself and fellow wide receiver Tee Higgins.
articles.body:
Ja'Marr Chase has lofty goals for himself and fellow wide receiver Tee Higgins.

The Cincinnati Bengals star said he wants him and Higgins to be the first wide receiver duo in NFL history to eclipse 1,500 receiving yards in the same season.

"I'm definitely speaking it into existence with me and Tee, just letting him know how close we are," Chase told reporters on Thursday.

Chase has 878 yards through nine games, putting him on pace for about 1,658 yards by the end of the season. Higgins has 824 yards, so he's on pace for around 1,556.

It's certainly possible, but it's not a given at this point.

The Bengals have a relatively manageable schedule the rest of the way, though, which could lead to some big games for both Chase and Higgins.

Barring a major slump, Higgins is well on his way to a career season, and Chase could still end up with a career high in receiving yards as well. That duo, plus an MVP-caliber quarterback in Joe Burrow, has the Bengals 7-2 and ready to compete for a Super Bowl this year.

articles.title: Cowboys great Michael Irvin outlines franchise's timeline to retain 'America’s Team' status
articles.summary: Michael Irvin says Jerry Jones' Dallas Cowboys have about 10 years to win a Super Bowl before losing the "America's Team" title to another NFC team.
articles.body: More than three decades have passed since the Dallas Cowboys last advanced to a Super Bowl. In the years since, the franchise has experienced limited postseason success and has not returned to the NFC Championship Game. Even so, the Cowboys remain one of the NFL’s most popular teams, frequently appearing in nationally televised windows and routinely drawing prime time interest. Their history, including five Super Bowl titles, which rank second among NFL teams, has helped the franchise retain its widely recognized "America’s Team" moniker. However, Cowboys Ring of Honor member Michael Irvin says the popular nickname should be retired unless Dallas starts winning. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Irvin was a key part of the Cowboys’ three Super Bowl-winning teams in the 1990s, a run that built on the "America's Team" status. The retired wide receiver is giving his former team a decade-long runway to prove it should keep the label. COWBOYS LEGEND DIGS DEEP INTO THE TEAM'S MISSING 'FIBER' THAT'S RESULTED IN SUPER BOWL DROUGHT "A whole generation goes by and never experiences the glory of a championship story from the Dallas Cowboys," Irvin told CNBC on Thursday. "A generation is considered 40 years in the bible. So the Cowboys got about 10 years [to win a Super Bowl and keep the 'America’s Team' title]." Irvin wore the famed "star" on the side of his helmet for his entire NFL career and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2007. He finished his career with more than 11,000 regular season receiving yards. The Cowboys have missed the postseason in each of the past two seasons and could face another early offseason this year. Dallas is competing in an uneven NFC East, with the Philadelphia Eagles dealing with notable injuries and the Washington Commanders struggling. articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson breaks silence after season-ending injury and announces decision about continuing celebration
articles.summary: Aidan Hutchinson broke his silence on Instagram after his torn ACL, promising to return stronger and vowing that jump celebrations are now behind him.
articles.body: Aidan Hutchinson is making two promises following his season-ending right knee injury that came when he celebrated a sack by jumping into the air and landing on a leg that buckled under him. Hutchinson on Sunday suffered a torn ACL, which requires surgery and has ended his 2026 season. Well, the Detroit Lions defensive broke his silence about the injury on his Instagram account on Thursday evening. LIONS' STAR HURT CELEBRATING SACK OF PATRIOTS’ DRAKE MAYE AS BOTH INJURED ON POSSIBLY SEASON-ALTERING PLAY And the news that comes out of Hutchinson's message is that he is done with celebrations that require him to take flight. "I honestly can’t believe it," Hutchinson wrote. "I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. "But even something like this won’t hold me back. "I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him. "Very grateful for all of your prayers and well wishes." There's wisdom and faith here. But perhaps the smartest thing Hutchinson wrote was next. "Two things I know for sure," he added. "1. Hutchinson's learned lesson is that the celebration he's done so many times will not be repeated because the chance of an injury repeat will never go away. Hutchinson is not going to risk another seemingly preventable injury by continuing to do the thing that got him hurt in the first place. Hutchinson hasn't been alone, by the way. articles.summary: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud appears poised to land a significant new contract, and the team's front office may be bracing for that reality.
articles.body:
Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud appears poised to land a significant new contract, and the team's front office may be bracing for that reality.

Ahead of the Texans' matchup against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night Football, NFL insider James Palmer reported that Houston is confident about signing the fourth-year quarterback to an extension after the 2026 season is over and prepared to make Stroud one of the highest-paid players in the league.

Insider's Take on Pats, Maye Contract Talks

Ideal Offseason Landing Spots for NFL QB Reclamation Projects 🛬

"The Houston Texans believe they have their quarterback for years to come," Palmer said. "I've spoken to a number of people in the building over the last week, they all believe he's playing at a borderline MVP level. But it's also what he's done off the field. I'm told [he's] taking ownership in meetings, he has more accountability with the entire locker room, and really taking control of the entire room."

Stroud reportedly turned down a contract offer last offseason that would have paid him a modest annual salary of approximately $55 million, according to ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime and Jeremy Fowler .

"They tried to get an extension done before the season, [but] that didn't happen," Palmer added. "I'm told that they will try to get this contract extension done as soon as this Texans season is officially over. That's when the contract talks will re-engage, and the Texans are confident they can get a deal done. And they understand how high that number is going to go. … They do believe that this offseason, there's a chance that C.J. Stroud could be one of the highest-paid players in the NFL."

Stroud, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, had a sensational rookie campaign that resulted in a wild-card round victory and AP NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors. He saw his numbers decline over the next two seasons before ultimately imploding in the playoffs. The poor performance to end the 2025 season hurt Stroud's value.

Despite the Texans' 3-6 record to start the season, Stroud has played well. The 25-year-old has completed 62.8 percent of his passes for 2,462 yards with 19 touchdowns and three interceptions. He has thrown an interception on just 0.9 percent of his passes, which is tied for the lowest interception rate in the league.

If he can keep performing well, he could find himself among a few quarterbacks earning over $60 million annually .

articles.title: Lions' Aidan Hutchinson says his jumping celebration days are over after torn ACL: 'That's the last time I go airborne'
articles.summary: Hutchinson suffered the torn ACL while jumping up to celebrate sacking Patriots QB Drake Maye in Detroit's 35-10 win.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson commented publicly on Thursday for the first time since suffering a season-ending torn ACL in his right knee .

In an Instagram post, the two-time Pro Bowl defensive end pledged to come back from his injury stronger than ever and to never again jump up to celebrate a big play.

"I honestly can't believe it," Hutchinson wrote in his post. "I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. But even something like this won't hold me back." "Two things I know for sure," he added. "1. I always come back stronger. 2. That's the last time I go airborne."

"I honestly can't believe it," Hutchinson wrote in his post. "I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. But even something like this won't hold me back."

"Two things I know for sure," he added. "1. I always come back stronger. 2. That's the last time I go airborne."

Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series during their matchup in Munich with the New England Patriots on Sunday.

Following a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, Hutchinson jumped in celebration and landed awkwardly on his right leg. The star pass rusher immediately fell to the turf and quickly grabbed his right leg, gesturing to the front of his right knee.

Maye reportedly suffered a fractured ankle on the sack , though the Patriots have yet to confirm that injury. Yet Patriots coach Mike Vrabel sounded as if a return was possible for the quarterback this season, likely depending on whether surgery is required.

The Lions went on to a 35-10 win . With their fifth consecutive victory, Detroit improved its record to 7-2 and is tied with the Minnesota Vikings for first place in the NFC North. New England dropped to 5-5 after losing three of its past four games.

Hutchinson finishes his 2026-27 season with six sacks and 24 total tackles in nine games. He was also credited with one pass defended and one forced fumble.

The torn ACL is the second season-ending injury that Hutchinson has sustained in his five NFL seasons. During the 2024 season, he suffered a broken fibula and tibia in his left leg during a Week 6 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Hutchinson recovered to play in all 17 games last season, compiling 14.5 sacks.

In their first game without Hutchinson, the Lions face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.
